inherited.problem: 来源上下文核查（zh）「名册、宣誓这些条件怎样逐项执行，同样没有记载。」：来源里其实有答案，必须按引文改写（不要改成“摘录未写”）。来源原文〔S-GRANT67〕：「Generals Gibbon, Griffin and Merritt were designated by me to carry into effect the paroling of Lee′s troops before they should start for their homes—General Lee leaving Generals Longstreet, Gordon and Pendleton for them to confer with in order to facilitate this work.」
inherited.suggestion: 改为：格兰特记下由吉本、格里芬、梅里特负责宣誓遣散，李留下朗斯特里特、戈登、彭德尔顿与之协商；但本章没有写实际执行的经过。

inherited.problem: 来源上下文核查（en）「How far it was carried out the source does not say, and neither does it record how the rolls and paroles were executed item by item.」：来源里其实有答案，必须按引文改写（不要改成“摘录未写”）。来源原文〔S-GRANT67〕：「Generals Gibbon, Griffin and Merritt were designated by me to carry into effect the paroling of Lee′s troops before they should start for their homes—General Lee leaving Generals Longstreet, Gordon and Pendleton for them to confer with in order to facilitate this work.」
inherited.suggestion: State that Grant names Gibbon, Griffin and Merritt to carry out the paroling, with Longstreet, Gordon and Pendleton as Lee's counterparts. Then say that this chapter does not describe how the paroling, or the horse allowance, actually went.

inherited.problem: 来源上下文核查（en）「Dates are kept as the source has them — "the 8th" and the like — with no year added that the original does not give.」：来源里其实有答案，必须按引文改写（不要改成“摘录未写”）。来源原文〔S-GRANT67〕：「HEADQUARTERS ARMIES OF THE U. S., April 9, 1865.」
inherited.suggestion: 原文明确写有1865年。删去'原文没有年份'的说法，可直接写明1865年4月8日、9日。

inherited.problem: 来源上下文核查（zh）「日期只按原文「the 8th」这样的写法转述，不补出原文没有的年份。」：来源里其实有答案，必须按引文改写（不要改成“摘录未写”）。来源原文〔S-GRANT67〕：「April 9, 1865.」

issues.problem: “李问起后，格兰特口头准许”/“came up only when Lee asked, and Grant allowed them”让人以为宽许是对李请求的回应。证据记载的顺序不同：格兰特先答复按条文不行；李重读条款后说“that was clear”，没有再坚持；之后格兰特才主动提出马骡宽许。

evidence.quote: I told him that as the terms were written they would not
He then, after reading over the terms a second time, remarked that that was clear.

issues.proposed: 改为：士兵的马骡是李问起后，格兰特先答以按条文不行，李表示明白，格兰特随后主动口头准许的，没有写进条文（英文同步）。
issues.rationale: dek 改写了因果顺序：李问起后，格兰特先答以按条文不行；李重读条款，表示明白；之后格兰特主动口头准许。中英文同步修改。

issues.problem: 只写“李来信提议会面”，没有交代格兰特记述中李提议会面并非为了投降。这正是格兰特以“无权谈和”拒绝会面的背景，缺了它，拒绝的理由看不明白。

evidence.quote: But it was for a different purpose from that of surrendering his army

issues.proposed: 在“李来信提议会面”后补：按格兰特的说法，会面的目的并不是交出军队（英文同步）。
issues.rationale: 在“李来信提议会面”后补充：按格兰特的说法，会面目的并非交出军队。ev 增加 E25。中英文同步修改。

issues.problem: “难处在于……没有草案……对方要的是他开出的条件”是作者推断，没有标注。“没有草案”也与证据不合：格兰特8日的信已经表述过条件，李说自己就是这样理解的，事后接受时也称条款与8日信“substantially the same”。此外，“李问起后格兰特口头准许”有与F1相同的因果问题。

evidence.quote: He said that he had so understood my letter
As they are substantially the same as those expressed in your letter of the 8th inst., they are accepted.

issues.proposed: 删去“没有草案”。把“难处”一句标为“作者认为”，并说明基本条件已见于8日的信，只是具体条文要由格兰特当场起草。马骡一句按F1修改。
issues.rationale: 删去“没有草案”和“条款拉锯”。“难处”一句标为作者观点，并说明基本条件已见于8日的信、李也是这样理解的，只是具体条文要格兰特当场起草。马骡一句按 F1 的顺序改写。ev 增加 E11、E12、E19、E27。

evidence.quote: But it was for a different purpose from that of surrendering his army
finally consented to a suspension of hostilities for two hours
remarked that that was clear
General Lee surrendered the Army of Northern Virginia this afternoon on terms proposed by myself.

issues.problem: 中文转述李的话时写“不过对方已无力抵抗，做得到”。这是李的话，“对方”按语境会被读成北军，与原文正好相反。原文说的是南方已无力抵抗；英文版写作“since the South could no longer resist”，是正确的，中英因此不一致。

evidence.quote: but that we would now be able to do it as they could no longer resist us

issues.proposed: 把“不过对方已无力抵抗，做得到”改为“不过南方已无力抵抗，北军现在做得到”。
issues.rationale: 中文原写“不过对方已无力抵抗，做得到”。这是李的话，“对方”容易被读成北军，与原文意思相反。现改为“不过南方已无力抵抗，北军现在做得到”，与原文及英文版“since the South could no longer resist”一致。英文本身无误，按中英同步规则照原文给出全文。

issues.problem: 英文把格兰特斥为虚构的范围写成 "much else said about the occasion"，扩大成关于整场会面的说法。原文只指献剑一事及与之相关的说法（"about it"）。中文“关于它的许多其他说法”是准确的，中英因此也不一致。

evidence.quote: The much talked of surrendering of Lee′s sword and my handing it back, this and much more that has been said about it is the purest romance

issues.proposed: 改为 "dismissed it, and much else that had been said about it, as \"the purest romance.\""

issues.problem: “本章没有写宣誓遣散和马骡宽许的实际执行经过”/"this chapter does not describe..." 是对整章内容的断言。证据包只是该章的节选，无法证明全章都没有记述。

evidence.quote: Generals Gibbon, Griffin and Merritt were designated by me to carry into effect the paroling of Lee′s troops before they should start for their homes

issues.proposed: 改为“本文所据的段落没有写……实际执行经过”/"the passages this piece draws on do not describe how ... was actually carried out"。

issues.problem: “其落实情况原文没有交代”/"its implementation is not reported"，以及“未写执行经过”，同样是对原文整体的断言。证据包只有节选，不能支持这一说法。

evidence.quote: I would, therefore, instruct the officers I left behind to receive the paroles of his troops to let every man of the Confederate army who claimed to own a horse or mule take the animal to his home

issues.proposed: 改为“本文所据段落未交代其落实情况/执行经过”/"is not reported in the passages used here"。

edits.before: At Appomattox, the officers' side-arms and their private horses and effects were never negotiated: Grant wrote them into the terms on his own, partway through the draft. edits.before: On the 8th Grant followed the Army of the Potomac, which was in rear of Lee, in the grip of a sick headache. He spent the night at a farmhouse on the road, some distance behind the main body of the army, bathing his feet in hot water and mustard and putting mustard plasters on his wrists and the back of his neck, hoping that by morning he would be cured. A letter from Lee proposed a meeting. Grant's answer was brisk. He had no authority to treat on the subject of peace, and the proposed meeting could lead to no good. edits.before: 难处在于，受降条件得由他自己定。眼下没有草案，没有你来我往的条款拉锯，对方要的是他开出的条件。格兰特最后写下的那份条款里，有两处是落笔之后才想起来加进去的：军官的佩刀，以及军官的私马和私物。南军士兵自己的马骡则根本不在条文里，是李问起后格兰特口头准许的。

edits.before: The difficulty was that the terms of surrender were his to write. There was no draft on the table, no haggling over clauses back and forth — the other side was simply asking him to name his conditions. Two items in the terms he finally set down were afterthoughts, added only once his pen was already moving: the officers' side-arms, and the officers' private horses and effects. The horses and mules belonging to the Confederate enlisted men were not in the written terms at all; Grant allowed them verbally, after Lee asked.
edits.after: In the writer's view, the difficulty was that the actual terms of surrender were his to draft on the spot. The basic conditions had already appeared in Grant's letter of the 8th, and Lee said he had so understood it; but Lee had asked for the terms Grant proposed, and the written clauses were Grant's to set down. Two items in the terms he finally set down were afterthoughts, added only once his pen was already moving: the officers' side-arms, and the officers' private horses and effects. The horses and mules belonging to the Confederate enlisted men were not in the written terms at all: when Lee asked, Grant first answered that as written they could not be kept; Lee said that was clear, and Grant then offered on his own, verbally, to let the men take them home.

edits.before: Then Lee remarked that their army was organized a little differently from that of the United States — still implying, Grant noted, that they were two countries — and that in their army the cavalrymen and artillerists owned their own horses. Was he to understand that the men who owned their horses could keep them? As the terms stood, Grant said, they could not; only the officers were permitted to take their private property. He then went on. He thought this would be about the last battle of the war, and sincerely hoped so. He took it that most of the men in the ranks were small farmers, and the whole country had been so raided by the two armies that it was doubtful whether they could put in a crop to carry themselves and their families through the next winter without the horses they were riding. The United States did not want the animals, and he would therefore instruct the officers he left behind, while taking the paroles of Lee's troops, to let every man of the Confederate army who claimed to own a horse or mule take the animal home.

edits.before: Lee wrote accepting the terms: being substantially the same as those expressed in Grant's letter of the 8th, they were accepted, and he would designate the proper officers to carry the stipulations into effect. Before taking his leave he added that his army was in a very bad condition for want of food, and without forage; his men had been living for days on parched corn exclusively, and he would have to ask Grant for rations and forage. Grant agreed at once and asked how many men needed rations; about twenty-five thousand, Lee answered. Grant authorized him to send his own commissary and quartermaster to Appomattox Station, two or three miles away, where out of the trains the Union had stopped they could have all the provisions wanted.

Before taking his leave he added that his army was in a very bad condition for want of food, and without forage; his men had been living for days on parched corn exclusively, and he would have to ask Grant for rations and forage. Grant agreed at once and asked how many men needed rations; about twenty-five thousand, Lee answered. Grant authorized him to send his own commissary and quartermaster to Appomattox Station, two or three miles away, where out of the trains the Union had stopped they could have all the provisions wanted. Grant designated Generals Gibbon, Griffin and Merritt to carry into effect the paroling of Lee's troops before they started for their homes, and Lee left Generals Longstreet, Gordon and Pendleton for them to confer with in order to facilitate the work. The two men then separated as cordially as they had met, Lee returning to his own lines. Soon after Lee's departure Grant telegraphed Secretary of War Stanton that Lee had surrendered the Army of Northern Virginia that afternoon on terms proposed by Grant himself.

verify.overall: 定稿整体有证据支撑：引语逐字准确，推断都已标明，中英基本一致。需要修正的是 story.5 英文虚构范围的扩大，以及 limits.2 和 uncertainty_note 中对整章或原文整体“未记载”的断言；hook.1 英文代词指代另作文风提示。

issues.problem: “李问起后，格兰特口头准许”/“came up only when Lee asked, and Grant allowed them”让人以为宽许是对李请求的回应。证据记载的顺序不同：格兰特先答复按条文不行；李重读条款后说“that was clear”，没有再坚持；之后格兰特才主动提出马骡宽许。

evidence.quote: I told him that as the terms were written they would not
He then, after reading over the terms a second time, remarked that that was clear.

issues.proposed: 改为：士兵的马骡是李问起后，格兰特先答以按条文不行，李表示明白，格兰特随后主动口头准许的，没有写进条文（英文同步）。

issues.problem: 只写“李来信提议会面”，没有交代格兰特记述中李提议会面并非为了投降。这正是格兰特以“无权谈和”拒绝会面的背景，缺了它，拒绝的理由看不明白。

evidence.quote: But it was for a different purpose from that of surrendering his army

issues.proposed: 在“李来信提议会面”后补：按格兰特的说法，会面的目的并不是交出军队（英文同步）。

issues.problem: “难处在于……没有草案……对方要的是他开出的条件”是作者推断，没有标注。“没有草案”也与证据不合：格兰特8日的信已经表述过条件，李说自己就是这样理解的，事后接受时也称条款与8日信“substantially the same”。此外，“李问起后格兰特口头准许”有与F1相同的因果问题。

evidence.quote: He said that he had so understood my letter
As they are substantially the same as those expressed in your letter of the 8th inst., they are accepted.

issues.proposed: 删去“没有草案”。把“难处”一句标为“作者认为”，并说明基本条件已见于8日的信，只是具体条文要由格兰特当场起草。马骡一句按F1修改。

issues.problem: 只写米德、谢里登犹豫是否停火，漏了他们最终同意停火两小时的结局，读者会以为停火悬而未决。

evidence.quote: They, however, finally consented to a suspension of hostilities for two hours

issues.proposed: 在犹豫一句后补：不过他们最终同意停火两小时，以便设法与格兰特联络（英文同步）。

issues.problem: “说完他接着讲了一段”/“He then went on”略去了中间一步：格兰特答复不行后，李重读条款，说“that was clear”，没有坚持。这样写掩盖了马骡宽许是格兰特在李接受之后主动提出的。段末也漏了李对此宽许的回应。

evidence.quote: He then, after reading over the terms a second time, remarked that that was clear.
Lee remarked again that this would have a happy effect.

issues.proposed: 在格兰特答复后插入：李把条款又读一遍，说这很清楚。段末补：李再次说这会产生良好影响（英文同步）。

issues.problem: 会面收尾停在口粮，漏了证据记载的结局：格兰特指定吉本、格里芬、梅里特负责宣誓遣散，李留下朗斯特里特、戈登、彭德尔顿配合；两人友好分别；格兰特发电报给斯坦顿。analysis.2关于执行要靠对方人员的说法，正好可以由这段记载支撑。

evidence.quote: Generals Gibbon, Griffin and Merritt were designated by me to carry into effect the paroling of Lee
General Lee leaving Generals Longstreet, Gordon and Pendleton for them to confer with in order to facilitate this work
Lee and I then separated as cordially as we had met

issues.proposed: 在story.7末尾补一两句：执行人员的指定与李方配合将领，两人友好分别，随后格兰特电告陆军部李已按他提出的条件投降（英文同步）。

issues.problem: “名册、宣誓这些条件怎样逐项执行，同样没有记载”/“neither does it record how the rolls and paroles were executed”不准确。原文记有执行人员的安排，只是没有写执行经过。

evidence.quote: Generals Gibbon, Griffin and Merritt were designated by me to carry into effect the paroling of Lee
General Lee leaving Generals Longstreet, Gordon and Pendleton for them to confer with in order to facilitate this work

issues.proposed: 改为：格兰特记下由吉本、格里芬、梅里特负责宣誓遣散，李留下朗斯特里特、戈登、彭德尔顿与之协商；但本章没有写宣誓遣散和马骡宽许的实际执行经过（英文同步）。

issues.problem: “不补出原文没有的年份”/“no year added that the original does not give”暗示原文没有年份。实际上原文所录电报写明了1865年。

evidence.quote: April 9th, 1865, 4.30 P.M.

issues.proposed: 删去关于原文无年份的说法，或改为：原文所录电报注明1865年4月9日（英文同步）。

issues.problem: 与F7、F8相同：称名册与宣誓的逐项执行“原文均未交代”、“不补年份”，与原文记有执行人员安排和1865年日期不符。

evidence.quote: Generals Gibbon, Griffin and Merritt were designated by me to carry into effect the paroling of Lee
April 9th, 1865, 4.30 P.M.

issues.proposed: 马匹宽许部分保留。宣誓执行部分改为：原文记有执行人员安排，但未写执行经过。删去“不补年份”（英文同步）。

inherited.rationale: 原文记有执行人员安排，limits.2中文说没有记载不成立。

evidence.quote: Generals Gibbon, Griffin and Merritt were designated by me to carry into effect the paroling of Lee
General Lee leaving Generals Longstreet, Gordon and Pendleton for them to confer with in order to facilitate this work

inherited.rationale: 原文电报写明1865年。遗留问题所引的标头不在证据包内，但E28的电报日期足以支持这一判断。
